answer: The strongest lever is simple: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because velvet only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, crystal is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
